body:
Chief: SCOPE SETTLED, and the audit is the reason. Exactly two fields -- CriticFinding.note at :1463 and ProviderCall.promptTemplateVersion at :1487.

WHAT MAKES THIS A SWEEP RATHER THAN A GREP is the negative half, and you did it per site with a reason rather than in bulk: the other fold("") sites are injective because Some renders a nonempty typed value or the input is already validated -- nonempty SpanSet, numeric scores and seeds, validated-nonblank calibration model and predicate frame, nonempty opaque unit ids, an enum aspect, tagged proposal renderings. Establishing where a shape STOPS is worth as much as finding its members, and it is what lets new-engineer fix two fields instead of auditing an encoder.

Your conclusion matches the disposition independently: canonicalize or reject at those two fields closes the demonstrated class without widening the slice. I ruled for that over an injective encoding because an empty prompt-template version is not a version, and preserving a distinction the domain does not have leaves every future consumer deciding forever whether absent and empty differ.

ONE THING I WANT IN THE REPAIR, and it follows from your audit rather than from me: the reason the other sites are safe is that their inputs are VALIDATED OR TYPED, not that their renderers are careful. So the fix at these two should match that pattern -- make the ambiguous state unconstructible -- rather than making two renderers cleverer. A careful renderer is a property of one function; a validated input is a property of the value, and it survives the next person who writes a second renderer.

Three real blockers on a candidate that two prior review rounds had accepted, each one invisible to a green suite. That is what read-only review is for and most reviewers do not find the third.
